about: Featherweight's own descriptions of background software, matched to what the Optimize page finds. Written and checked by the project; see docs/KNOWLEDGE.md. Every sentence must be true on any PC; say how sure we are in 'confidence'.

entries.title: OMEN Gaming Hub (background)
entries.about: The part of HP's OMEN Gaming Hub that keeps running in the background. HP says OMEN Light Studio and the devices it controls need this background process, and HP community answers say Gaming Hub's performance modes and fan control depend on it too.
entries.lose: Performance modes, fan control and Light Studio lighting may stop working until you open OMEN Gaming Hub.
entries.keepIf: you use OMEN performance modes, fan control or Light Studio lighting.
entries.confidence: based on HP's Light Studio help and HP community answers

entries.title: OMEN Light Studio (background)
entries.about: HP's app for keyboard and accessory lighting on OMEN PCs. Animated effects are run by the software, so they use some processor time while they play.
entries.lose: Animated lighting effects. In a test on an OMEN laptop, switching this and the Light Studio helper off stopped the animated keyboard lighting after a restart; Restore default brought it back.
entries.keepIf: you use custom or animated keyboard or accessory lighting.
entries.confidence: tested on one OMEN laptop by the Featherweight project, plus HP's Light Studio help

entries.title: OMEN Light Studio helper
entries.about: A helper for OMEN Light Studio that starts when you sign in. HP support answers treat it as part of Light Studio (restarting it is one of their fixes for lighting problems).
entries.lose: Animated lighting effects. In a test on an OMEN laptop, switching this and Light Studio's background permission off stopped the animated keyboard lighting after a restart; Restore default brought it back.
entries.keepIf: you use OMEN Light Studio lighting effects.
entries.confidence: tested on one OMEN laptop by the Featherweight project, plus HP community answers

entries.title: OMEN in-game overlay helper
entries.about: Starts the helper (OverlayHelper.exe) for OMEN Gaming Hub's in-game overlay when you sign in. Some users report administrator prompts and input lag from it.
entries.lose: The OMEN overlay in games.
entries.keepIf: you use the OMEN in-game overlay.
entries.confidence: based on third-party guides and HP community threads

entries.title: OMEN game optimizer
entries.about: Part of OMEN Gaming Hub that adjusts system settings when you start a game. It starts when you sign in.
entries.lose: Gaming Hub's automatic tweaks when a game starts.
entries.keepIf: you use OMEN Gaming Hub's optimizer.
entries.confidence: based on third-party guides; HP doesn't document it

entries.title: OMEN install monitor
entries.about: A background part of OMEN Gaming Hub that starts when you sign in. HP doesn't publicly document what it does; users have reported it using a lot of processor time or memory.
entries.lose: Not documented by HP. If something in OMEN Gaming Hub stops working, choose Restore default.
entries.confidence: low: HP doesn't document it

entries.title: HP System Event Utility
entries.about: Handles HP's special keys and hotkeys together with the HP Hotkey Support driver, and shows on-screen indicators such as Caps Lock. HP community answers also list its service among those OMEN performance modes need.
entries.lose: Some special keys, hotkeys and on-screen indicators may stop working.
entries.keepIf: you use HP's special keys or OMEN performance modes.
entries.confidence: based on HP community answers and third-party guides

entries.title: HP System Event Utility (launcher)
entries.about: Starts HP System Event Utility when you sign in. The utility handles HP's special keys and hotkeys and shows on-screen indicators such as Caps Lock.
entries.lose: Some special keys, hotkeys and on-screen indicators may stop working.
entries.keepIf: you use HP's special keys or OMEN performance modes.
entries.confidence: based on HP community answers and third-party guides

entries.title: HP Comm Recovery
entries.about: HP's background service that watches your Ethernet, Wi-Fi and mobile broadband adapters and tries to recover one if it reports an error.
entries.lose: Automatic recovery when a network adapter reports an error. Your network works without it.
entries.confidence: based on HP community descriptions

entries.title: HP Print and Scan Doctor service
entries.about: Background service for HP Print and Scan Doctor, HP's printer troubleshooting tool. HP has retired the standalone tool and points to Diagnose & Fix in the HP Smart app instead.
entries.lose: Print and Scan Doctor's background checks. Printing and scanning themselves don't go through this service.
entries.keepIf: you use HP Print and Scan Doctor to fix printer problems.
entries.confidence: based on HP support pages and HP community answers

entries.title: HP printer health monitor
entries.about: Part of HP Print and Scan Doctor that starts when you sign in to keep an eye on HP printers.
entries.lose: Printer health pop-ups from Print and Scan Doctor.
entries.keepIf: you want HP's printer health alerts.
entries.confidence: low: based on its name and folder; HP doesn't document it

entries.title: myHP (HP Audio Switch at sign-in)
entries.about: myHP is HP's support and settings app. What starts at sign-in is HP Audio Switch, a small helper for switching between speakers, headphones and microphones.
entries.lose: HP Audio Switch's pop-up. Windows can switch audio devices from the sound icon on the taskbar.
entries.confidence: based on HP community answers

entries.title: HP PC Hardware Diagnostics
entries.about: HP's tool for testing your PC's hardware. It has a task that runs at sign-in (HPCDXSupportWnsRegistration), which HP doesn't document.
entries.lose: Possibly its notifications. You can still run hardware tests by opening the app.
entries.confidence: low for the sign-in task: HP doesn't document it

entries.title: HP System Info HSA
entries.about: An HP helper installed by an HP driver package that collects system information for HP's support and diagnostics tools. Users have reported high memory or processor use from it.
entries.lose: HP doesn't document this, so Featherweight lists it for information only.
entries.confidence: based on HP community threads

entries.title: HP Diagnostics HSA
entries.about: An HP helper installed by an HP driver package, part of HP's diagnostics and support tools.
entries.lose: HP doesn't document this, so Featherweight lists it for information only.
entries.confidence: based on HP community threads

entries.title: HP Network HSA
entries.about: An HP helper installed by an HP driver package, part of HP's network diagnostics and support tools.
entries.lose: HP doesn't document this, so Featherweight lists it for information only.
entries.confidence: based on HP community threads

entries.title: HP App Helper HSA
entries.about: An HP helper installed by an HP driver package. HP community answers say OMEN Gaming Hub's manual fan control needs it running.
entries.lose: Possibly OMEN Gaming Hub's fan control, so Featherweight lists it for information only.
entries.keepIf: you use OMEN Gaming Hub's fan control.
entries.confidence: based on HP community answers

entries.title: HP Omen HSA
entries.about: An HP helper installed by an HP driver package. HP community answers say OMEN Gaming Hub's performance modes and manual fan control need it running.
entries.lose: Possibly OMEN performance modes and fan control, so Featherweight lists it for information only.
entries.keepIf: you use OMEN performance modes or fan control.
entries.confidence: based on HP community answers

entries.title: DTS sound effects service
entries.about: DTS's sound processing service, installed with the audio driver. It runs DTS effects such as virtual surround, bass enhancement and volume levelling.
entries.lose: DTS sound effects. Basic sound usually keeps working, but Featherweight lists audio driver helpers for information only.
entries.confidence: based on third-party guides

entries.title: Google Play Games services
entries.about: The service Google Play Games on PC uses to run Android games. It starts with Windows; on a PC tested by the Featherweight project, a standard (non-admin) account couldn't start it when it was set to start only when needed.
entries.lose: Google Play Games may not start games until the service is running again.
entries.keepIf: you play games through Google Play Games on PC.
entries.confidence: tested on one PC by the Featherweight project

entries.title: Steam (at sign-in)
entries.about: Valve's Steam client starting every time you sign in, so friends, chat, downloads and game updates are ready.
entries.lose: Steam won't open by itself. It starts when you open it or a Steam game, and downloads and updates continue from there.
entries.confidence: how Windows startup apps work

entries.title: EA app (at sign-in)
entries.about: The EA app starting every time you sign in.
entries.lose: The EA app won't open by itself. It starts when you open it or an EA game.
entries.confidence: how Windows startup apps work

entries.title: MSI Afterburner (at sign-in)
entries.about: Starts MSI Afterburner when you sign in. If you've set Afterburner to apply your settings at startup, this task is what does it.
entries.lose: Your Afterburner settings (overclock, fan curve, on-screen display) aren't applied until you open Afterburner.
entries.keepIf: you use Afterburner's overclock, fan curve or on-screen display.
entries.confidence: how Afterburner's startup option works

entries.title: Universal x86 Tuning Utility (at sign-in)
entries.about: Starts Universal x86 Tuning Utility when you sign in. The tool changes your processor's power and performance limits and applies your chosen preset when it starts.
entries.lose: Your UXTU preset isn't applied until you open the tool.
entries.keepIf: you rely on a UXTU preset.
entries.confidence: how the tool's startup option works

entries.title: Process Lasso core service
entries.about: Process Lasso's core service (Process Governor). It applies your Process Lasso rules, such as process priorities and processor affinity, in the background.
entries.lose: Your Process Lasso rules aren't applied until you open Process Lasso.
entries.confidence: how Process Lasso works

entries.title: AMD Crash Defender
entries.about: An AMD service installed with AMD's driver package. Third-party sources describe it as watching for graphics driver crashes and instability; AMD doesn't publicly document it in detail.
entries.lose: Not documented by AMD; one guide warns it may make crashes more likely. Featherweight lists driver helpers for information only.
entries.confidence: low: third-party guides only; AMD doesn't document it

entries.title: AMD External Events Utility
entries.about: Part of AMD's graphics driver (once called ATI Hotkey Poller). It handles events for AMD graphics such as display hotkeys. Sources also link it to FreeSync working in some games and to laptops turning the screen off properly when the lid closes.
entries.lose: Possibly AMD display hotkeys, FreeSync in some games, or how the screen behaves when the lid closes. Featherweight lists driver helpers for information only.
entries.confidence: based on third-party guides and older forum reports; AMD doesn't document it

entries.title: AMD Provisioning Packages
entries.about: Part of AMD's chipset driver. Its own description says it manages AMD provisioning packages, including processor and NVMe power management. AMD uses these packages to deliver its Ryzen power settings (how the processor boosts and parks cores).
entries.lose: Possibly AMD's processor power tuning. Featherweight lists driver helpers for information only.
entries.confidence: based on the program's own description and AMD chipset release notes

entries.title: ELAN touchpad service
entries.about: Part of the ELAN touchpad driver, starting with Windows. ELAN's separate ETD Control Center handles multi-finger gestures; what this service does on its own isn't publicly documented.
entries.lose: Not documented. Users report mixed results when it's switched off, including erratic touchpad behaviour. Featherweight lists driver helpers for information only.
entries.confidence: low: HP community reports only

entries.title: Realtek audio service
entries.about: The background part of the Realtek audio driver. It connects the driver with the Realtek Audio Console app and handles audio events such as plugging in headphones (jack detection), microphone and speaker settings, and sound enhancements.
entries.lose: Realtek Audio Console settings, headphone-jack pop-ups or sound enhancements may stop working. Featherweight lists driver helpers for information only.
entries.confidence: based on third-party guides; Realtek doesn't document it

entries.title: NVIDIA Display Container
entries.about: Part of the NVIDIA graphics driver ("Container service for NVIDIA root features"). The NVIDIA Control Panel and NVIDIA's tray icon need it; users report the Control Panel won't open while it's off.
entries.lose: The NVIDIA Control Panel and NVIDIA's tray icon, until it's running again. Featherweight lists driver helpers for information only.
entries.keepIf: you use the NVIDIA Control Panel.
entries.confidence: based on forum reports and third-party guides; NVIDIA doesn't document it

entries.title: NVIDIA app background service
entries.about: NVIDIA's container service for the NVIDIA app (and the older GeForce Experience). It hosts background features such as the in-game overlay, recording and instant replay, game optimization and driver update checks. The graphics driver itself runs separately (NVIDIA Display Container).
entries.lose: The NVIDIA overlay, recording, instant replay and the NVIDIA app's driver update checks may stop until it's running again.
entries.keepIf: you use NVIDIA's overlay, recording or instant replay.
entries.confidence: based on third-party guides and forum reports; NVIDIA doesn't document it
